```{r data generation, echo = FALSE, results = "hide"}
n <- sample(20:50, 1)
xbar <- sample(60:90, 1)
s <- sample(5:15, 1)

se <- s / sqrt(n)
```

Question
========

A random sample of size $n=`r n`$ was obtained from a population. The sample mean was $\bar{x}=`r xbar`$ and the sample standard deviation was $s=`r s`$.

Compute the standard error of the sample mean using

$$
SE(\bar{x})=\frac{s}{\sqrt{n}}.
$$

Round your answer to two decimal places.

Solution
========

Using

$$
SE(\bar{x})=\frac{s}{\sqrt{n}},
$$

we obtain

$$
SE(\bar{x})=
\frac{`r s`}{\sqrt{`r n`}}
=
`r round(se,2)`.
$$
